domestic.debt_note: Re-verified this run: SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% on 2026-07-27 (second consecutive hold, first FY27 decision); next MPC confirmed 2026-09-14 (https://dunyanews.tv/en/Business/964879-sbp-keeps-policy-rate-unchanged-at-1150pc, https://www.momentumpakistan.com/blog/breaking-sbp-keeps-rate-unchanged-at-115-to-start-fy27-second-consecutive-hold-2026-07-27-16-31-54-nqetatkdhn-71057). 6M T-bill cutoff reconfirmed at 11.79% (2026-07-23 auction: 1M 11.35%, 3M 11.51%, 12M 11.99%, Rs768bn raised), still ~30bp above the held policy rate -- no fresher auction this run (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017647/govt-raises-rs768bn-via-treasury-bills-auction, https://pkrevenue.com/pakistan-treasury-bill-yields-fall-to-four-year-low-return-to-single-digits/). 10Y PIB carried forward at 11.69% -- no fresher PIB auction found this run. IMF: 3rd EFF/2nd RSF review board-completed 2026-05-08 (~$1.3bn disbursed, cumulative ~$4.8bn); next mission (4th review, likely combined with Article IV) still only guided to 'H2 2026' with no confirmed date as of this run's search (https://www.imf.org/en/countries/pak, https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf). June CPI actual print (latest official) was 11.1% YoY (https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2649243/pakistan); July brokerage forecasts (Growth Securities, JS Global -- estimates, not an official print) put July CPI near 9.1% YoY, still above the FY27 8.2% average target, with both houses flagging renewed Middle East tension as the key upside risk; official PBS print due 2026-08-01 (https://pakistan.shafaqna.com/EN/331621).
domestic.remittances: Reconfirmed this run, no fresher print: June 2026 remittances were $3.5bn (+2% YoY but -18.3% MoM from May's record $4.25bn); FY26 full year closed at a record $41.6bn (+8.6% YoY, +$3.3bn vs FY25's $38.3bn), with SBP incentive schemes for the corridor now ended (https://www.geo.tv/latest/672203-workers-remittances-rise-86-to-416bn-in-fy26, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429234/overseas-pakistanis-send-416bn-in-fy26-as-sbp-ends-incentive-schemes).
domestic.current_account: Reconfirmed this run, no fresher print: June 2026 current account swung to a $649mn monthly deficit (from May's $500mn surplus) as imports rose 9% MoM to $6.14bn against lower remittances, closing FY26 at a marginal $139mn full-year deficit despite record remittances (https://dailytimes.com.pk/1524687/pakistan-posts-139m-current-account-deficit-despite-record-remittances-in-fy26/, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40430638/fy26-ca-posts-usd139m-deficit). SBP reserves reconfirmed at $17.26bn (+$33mn w/w) for the week ended 2026-07-17 -- the prior week (ended 2026-07-10) had fallen $1.24bn on debt repayments, so the trajectory remains choppy; next weekly print (week ended ~2026-07-24) due 2026-07-31, not yet published as of this run (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619918/sbp-reserves-rise-33m-to-1726b, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618658/reserves-down-124b-on-debt-repayments).

global_read: global.json (17:37) shows the acute oil spike still fading day to day -- Brent -1.58% to $86.96 (still +18.88% over 1mo), WTI -1.32% to $81.52 (+15.22% 1mo) -- while VIX ticked up to 18.76 (+0.48% 1d, +6.29% 1mo), S&P/Dow both modestly positive, gold soft (-1.03% 1d), and USD/PKR a touch weaker at 277.75 with DXY flat. Net: stabilizing but not resolved -- the 1-month base for oil and vol stays elevated even as the daily tape calms, a mixed backdrop for PSX rather than a clean tailwind.
drivers: SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight meeting on 2026-07-27, confirming the next MPC for 2026-09-14 -- removes near-term rate uncertainty and keeps T-bill/PIB yields (11.79%/11.69%) attractively above the policy floor for banks, but the hold itself was pre-flagged/expected and is not a fresh catalyst (https://dunyanews.tv/en/Business/964879-sbp-keeps-policy-rate-unchanged-at-1150pc, https://www.momentumpakistan.com/blog/breaking-sbp-keeps-rate-unchanged-at-115-to-start-fy27-second-consecutive-hold-2026-07-27-16-31-54-nqetatkdhn-71057)

Market action over the last two sessions shows the SBP-hold-plus-oil-relief-plus-refinery-policy story has already been substantially priced: KSE-100 surged +4.23% (7,241pts) to 178,262.34 on 2026-07-27 on the SBP hold and Iran de-escalation signal easing oil pressure, then on 2026-07-28 opened firmer on the Cabinet's approval of Brownfield Refining Policy amendments (Euro-V mandate, Gulf investment roadshows) but faded to -0.16% (177,982.68) by midday as refinery names specifically came under pressure over the contested cut to deemed-duty protection (7.5% to 5%) -- a 'sell the news' pattern, not fresh broad conviction (https://mettisglobal.news/PSX-Closing-Bell-Good-Times-Roll-62172, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620725/psx-slips-into-negative-territory-amid-cautious-trading, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620714/cabinet-approves-amendments-to-oil-refining-policy-for-euro-v-fuel-rollout)

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, 17:37) reads 63/100 'moderate' with conflict/escalation stress pinned at 100 and energy-shock stress at 83 -- the Middle East risk premium underlying oil's elevated 1-month base has not genuinely cleared even as the daily tape eases (state/georisk.json)

External accounts stay fragile: FY26 current account closed at a $139mn deficit despite record $41.6bn remittances, June alone swung to a $649mn deficit on a 9% import jump, and SBP reserves ($17.26bn) are on a choppy week-to-week path rather than a clean build -- a headwind for PKR stability that keeps SBP cautious on any future easing (https://dailytimes.com.pk/1524687/pakistan-posts-139m-current-account-deficit-despite-record-remittances-in-fy26/, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619918/sbp-reserves-rise-33m-to-1726b)

The first hard read on how the recent oil whipsaw feeds through to prices is still pending: June CPI was 11.1% YoY (official, PBS), and brokerage estimates (not an official print) put July near 9.1% YoY, still above the FY27 8.2% target -- official PBS print due 2026-08-01 (https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2649243/pakistan, https://pakistan.shafaqna.com/EN/331621)

IMF program remains on track but with no fresh catalyst this run: 3rd EFF/2nd RSF review board-completed 2026-05-08 (~$1.3bn disbursed, cumulative ~$4.8bn); next mission (4th review + likely Article IV) still only guided to 'H2 2026' with no date confirmed (https://www.imf.org/en/countries/pak)

favored: banks (T-bill/PIB yields still above the held 11.5% policy rate; SBP hold removes near-term uncertainty; S&P sovereign upgrade to 'B' on 2026-07-22 is a direct credit-quality tailwind, carried forward)
E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI -- oil's 1-month base remains structurally elevated even after the daily pullback; net beneficiary of any residual Middle East risk premium)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta)
avoid: refineries (ATRL/NRL/PRL/Cnergyico) -- the Brownfield Refining Policy amendments approved 2026-07-28 are a real catalyst (Euro-V mandate, Gulf investment roadshows) but the sector itself sold off intraday today on the contested deemed-duty cut (7.5% to 5%), so near-term price action argues caution even as the medium-term policy backdrop improves
OMCs (current account still in deficit; a whipsawing oil tape compounds margin-timing/circular-debt risk on fuel-price pass-through)
autos (imported-input cost + inflation-pressured consumer demand, policy rate still restrictive)
textiles/exporters (current account swung to deficit in June; Red Sea/Middle East freight and insurance risk stays live via conflict/escalation stress pinned at 100 on the geo-risk radar)
